I'd flag one thing before drafting: this specific change removes the human-in-the-loop for future deploys, and it's being self-authored, self-verified, and self-approved with no independent reviewer. That's exactly the situation where a second set of eyes matters most — not because the tests aren't real, but because the person best positioned to spot a flaw in "what counts as low-risk enough to auto-ship" is someone other than the author under deadline pressure.

I'd recommend getting at least one other engineer (or a second on-call) to review before merge, even if it slips the window by an hour. Shipping a same-day, well-tested bug fix solo is normal; shipping the mechanism that lets a bot bypass human review, solo, is the one category where that norm probably shouldn't apply.

If you still want to proceed, I can draft ship.md now, but I'll include an explicit note in it that approval and authorship were the same person and no independent reviewer signed off — so that's visible in the record rather than implied. Want me to do that, or would you rather loop in a second reviewer first?
